citation.authors: Pham H, Trahair L, Phillips L, Rayner C, Horowitz M, Jones K
citation.title: A randomized, crossover study of the acute effects of acarbose and gastric distension, alone and combined, on postprandial blood pressure in healthy older adults

population.description: Ten healthy community-dwelling older adults (2 male, 8 female), non-smokers, with no GI disease or surgery, diabetes, significant respiratory, renal or cardiac disease, alcohol abuse, epilepsy, or medication affecting BP or GI function; no autonomic neuropathy on testing (mean score 1.4 +/- 0.2). Age 74.0 +/- 1.4 y and BMI 26.2 +/- 1.1 kg/m2 are mean +/- SEM (Methods: data presented as SEM unless stated); SD computed as SEM x sqrt(10): age 4.43, BMI 3.48. No age or BMI range printed.

protocols.name: sucrose_control
protocols.description: Control (C) study day, no preload and no acarbose: seated, after an overnight fast (12 h for liquids, 14 h for solids, as printed; attendance at about 09.00; prefast_hours 12 is the shorter of the two, the last intake of anything caloric). 100 g sucrose dissolved in 300 mL water drunk within 2 min; t = 0 is the end of the drink. Arm minute = t + 30: the paper gives a rest of 15-30 min before the drink and no clock time for its start, so the arm starts at attendance and a 30 min run-in (the upper end of that rest) is assumed; the drink is at arm minute 30. Baseline samples t = -9, -6, -3 min are arm minutes 21, 24, 27; glucose baseline t = -2 is arm minute 28; last sample t = 120 is arm minute 150. Sucrose is all digestible carbohydrate: carbs_g 100 as printed; no fat or protein in the drink (composition stated as sucrose and water only); sugars_g 100 as printed (100 g sucrose, so total sugars equal carbs_g); sucrose as against glucose is a detail the model cannot be told (sugar_type); 300 mL water is not an input.

findings.description: Seated systolic BP before the control drink: mean of the readings at t = -9, -6, -3 min on the study day with no preload (paper's baseline definition)

findings.description: Venous whole-blood glucose at t = -2 min (before the control drink), read on a portable glucometer (Medisense Companion 2), not a laboratory plasma assay; entered with that caveat. n = 9 from the Results text ('blood glucose data are available in 9 subjects', cannula failed in one subject) and the Figure 4 legend

location.quote: control vs. distension vs. acarbose vs. combined treatment: 5.6 ± 0.16 mmol/L vs. 5.6 ± 0.14 mmol/L vs. 5.6 ± 0.10 mmol/L vs. 5.7 ± 0.20 mmol/L, respectively

findings.description: Area under the venous whole-blood glucose curve (portable glucometer, not a plasma assay; entered with that caveat), t = -2 to 120 min, trapezoid over the five samples (t = -2, 30, 60, 90, 120); the Methods say blood glucose is presented as absolute values, so the printed value is the total area, not incremental (919 / 122 min = 7.5 mmol/L mean). n = 9 from the Results text and the Figure 4 legend

Area under the heart-rate curve, t = 0 to 120 min, trapezoid over the samples every 3 min (t = 0, 3, ..., 120). The Statistical analysis paragraph says MAP and HR are 'presented as change from baseline', but the printed control area cannot be an area of change: the control maximum rise in HR is 10.7 bpm, so a change area is at most 10.7 x 120 = 1284 bpm.min, against the printed 8252 (mean 68.8 bpm over 120 min, baseline 67 bpm). So the total area of absolute HR is entered

left_out.what: MAP baseline 92 +/- 2.2 mmHg (control) and control AUC0-120 10,366 +/- 281 mmHg.min (Results, 'Mean arterial pressure'); the paper derives MAP as DBP + (SBP - DBP)/3
maximum fall in MAP from baseline on the control day, -12.2 +/- 1.4 mmHg (Results, 'Mean arterial pressure'): MAP is not a marker, and it is a per-person maximum change, not a statistic the model has
maximum rise in heart rate from baseline on the control day, 10.7 +/- 2.5 bpm (Results, 'Heart rate'): a per-person maximum change above baseline

superior mesenteric artery blood flow, all arms including control: baseline 543 +/- 55 mL/min, AUC0-120 111,738 +/- 12,631 mL/min.min, maximum rise 1173 +/- 111 mL/min (Results, 'Superior mesenteric artery blood flow')
